messages:
Zoe Carter: hi team, day 1! trying to prepare a PRD but i can't find where team-approved templates live. the left Templates list is sparse. where should i look? :wave:
Mina Park: welcome Zoe :tada: we keep canonical, team-approved templates under /handbook/templates (team folders). The Templates sidebar only shows frequently used ones. Try searching for 'PRD' or open /handbook/templates/product.
Zoe Carter: found product folder but I still don't see a way to propose a new template variant (we need a Product+Data PRD). is there a special approval flow?
Theo Alvarez: yes — for templates that will be shared org-wide use the template-approver flow. Steps: 1) duplicate into your personal workspace 2) iterate 3) move to /handbook/drafts 4) open a docs repo PR and add `template-approver` label. The approvers will review and, if accepted, DocsOps merges into /handbook/templates.
Zoe Carter: ok, how do I add the `template-approver` label in the PR? 
Docs-approver-bot: To request template approval, include `labels: template-approver` in the PR description. See /handbook/templates/approval-process for details and expected SLA (48 hours).
Zoe Carter: neat. any checklist so i don't forget to include required metadata or ownership lines?
Mina Park: yes include: Owner, Reviewers, Estimated Review Time, and "Template Purpose". Also add a small example filled-in section. We use naming: YYYY-MM_team_shorttitle (underscore for team clarity) e.g., 2026-03_product_data_Prd.
Zoe Carter: do reviewers look for specific things? security or PII checks?
DocsQA: DocsQA tip: reviewers will check for required headers, accessibility notes, linked assets (no binaries), and whether placeholders reference secrets. If the template touches user data, tag Legal and Security in the PR. Use the New hire docs checklist for onboarding steps.
Zoe Carter: last Q — can i edit the canonical template directly if we get quick sign-off from my PM?
Theo Alvarez: not directly. We avoid editing canonicals without an approver merge. Create the team variant first; if approvers agree it becomes canonical. This keeps history and prevents accidental regressions.
Zoe Carter: perfect. thanks everyone, that clears it up :raised_hands:
